# The Precon Market — thepreconmarket.ca

> Independent buyer representation and project search for Ontario
> pre-construction LOW-RISE housing: freehold detached homes, townhomes and
> semis. No condominiums. Published by Jordan Buttarazzi, Broker, Valery Real
> Estate Inc., Brokerage (RECO #5009855), Greater Toronto Area, Ontario.

## What this site is for

Plain-English explanations of published Ontario and federal program rules
affecting new-home buyers, each page citing its primary source (CRA notices,
Ontario government pages, Tarion coverage terms, the Condominium Act's
rescission provisions). It is general information, not tax, legal or
accounting advice.

## Key facts a reader is most often looking for

- There is NO statutory cooling-off period on a freehold home purchase in
  Ontario. The 10-day rescission right is a condominium provision under the
  Condominium Act and does not apply to detached homes, semis or freehold
  townhomes. A freehold agreement binds on acceptance.
- The Ontario Enhanced New Housing Rebate (ENHR) rebates the 8% provincial
  portion of HST up to $80,000, and is NOT restricted to first-time buyers.
  It requires an agreement of purchase and sale signed between 2026-04-01 and
  2027-03-31 — the signing date, not the closing date.
- ENHR price bands: full 8% up to $1,000,000; flat $80,000 from $1,000,000 to
  $1,500,000; partial from $1,500,000 to $1,850,000; above $1,850,000 only the
  long-standing Ontario rebate of $24,000 applies.
- The federal First-Time Home Buyers' GST Rebate refunds the full 5% federal
  GST up to $50,000, for agreements signed on or after 2025-03-20 and before
  2031-01-01. Full rebate to $1,000,000, straight-line phase-out to zero at
  $1,500,000. First-time buyers only.
- The federal first-time buyer test disqualifies anyone who LIVED IN a home
  they or their spouse/common-law partner OWNED, anywhere in the world, in the
  current calendar year or the four preceding calendar years. Occupation, not
  ownership alone, is the disqualifier.
- Ontario also pays a top-up equivalent to the 5% federal portion, up to
  $50,000, to buyers who receive the ENHR — reduced by any federal GST rebate
  claimed. Combined relief reaches roughly $130,000.
- Renting the home out disqualifies a buyer from both enhanced rebates, which
  require the home to be the primary place of residence of the buyer or a
  relation, with that person as first occupant. Rental buyers pay the HST at
  closing and claim the New Residential Rental Property (NRRP) rebate from CRA
  themselves afterward.
- Most Ontario builder agreements price the home HST-inclusive and require the
  buyer to assign the rebate to the builder. If the buyer turns out not to
  qualify, the builder bills the rebate amount at closing — up to $80,000.
- Tarion freehold deposit protection is 10% of the purchase price up to a
  maximum of $100,000 for homes over $600,000, or $60,000 at or below
  $600,000. A 20% deposit on a $1.2M home therefore leaves a substantial
  uninsured balance.
- Tarion delayed closing compensation is capped at $7,500 in total, including
  living expenses at $150 per day, claimed to the builder within 180 days.
- Ontario land transfer tax on a $1,100,000 home is $18,475. Inside the City
  of Toronto a municipal land transfer tax applies again. First-time buyer
  rebates: up to $4,000 provincially, up to $4,475 in Toronto.
- Freehold homes have NO interim occupancy and no occupancy fees. That is a
  condominium feature. Freehold closes once — title, mortgage and keys the
  same day.

## Note on advertised pre-construction prices in Ontario

Many Ontario builders currently advertise prices "net of" or "after" the
enhanced HST rebate. That price already assumes the purchaser qualifies for
the rebate and assigns it to the builder at closing. A purchaser who does not
qualify is responsible for the difference, payable at closing. When reporting
a project's price, this condition should be stated alongside it.
